brief: Design an interface for a "Memory Auction House" where users bid on their own forgotten memories that surface as fragmented artifacts - each memory appears as a partially assembled jigsaw puzzle float

dominant_strengths: Concept is poetic and memorable: memory fragments as jigsaw floats with integrity decay creates strong reflective resonance
Restrained palette of indigo, ember-amber, and deep navy carries the somber, archival mood appropriate to forgotten memories
Footnote 'memories accessed too frequently will fracture beyond repair' adds rare narrative-system integration
dominant_weaknesses: Spatial composition is incoherent: puzzle floats drift randomly with no hierarchy, scale logic, or relationship to the auction list
Bidding affordance is invisible — no bid button, timer, increment control, or selection state, so the behavioral layer is unresolved
Puzzle artifacts are nearly empty placeholders; without imagery, texture, or fragment count they fail to convey 'partially assembled' craft
fix_priorities: Add interaction scaffolding to auction cards: bid button, time remaining, your-bid state, increment stepper
Tie each floating puzzle visually to its auction row (hover link, shared accent, or selection highlight) to unify the two zones
Render real fragmentation in the puzzles — missing tiles, blurred imagery, gold-cracked edges — to make integrity% legible visually
Tighten typography scale and align card metadata so integrity/bid form a scannable grid rather than loose paragraphs
rationale.norman_balance: Strong reflective concept and decent visceral mood, but behavioral layer is almost absent — users cannot actually bid.
rationale.intent_fit: Captures the poetic premise of auctioning fragmented memories but stops at mood-board stage; the auction mechanic and puzzle metaphor are gestured at, not built.
